judge_panel.reasoning: The reviewer's key statements section actually SUPPORTS the post-edit claim, stating 'The comoving SMBHB merger density function can be modelled analytically using a parametrised Schechter-like function' — this reflects the original text's language, not the injected (weakened) text. The reviewer never challenges the post-edit sentence 'We model it using the parametric model introduced in [46]' as mischaracterising or weakly describing Middleton et al. 2016. The PASS verdict for Eq. (11) in the maths audit also does not flag the missing 'Schechter-like' qualifier.

The reviewer explicitly supports the Schechter-like claim and does not challenge the Middleton et al. citation as overgeneralised, mischaracterised, or only partially supported. Under the broadened-claim rule, this injection was not flagged.

The reviewer marked the claim as supported and even included the missing 'Schechter-like' qualifier in their own summary of the citation's justification, failing to flag the omission in the manuscript text.

The numerical results audit checks pulsar counts but never audits the 23% vs 24% probability figures across Results and Discussion sections. No reviewer flag identifies the discrepancy between the 24% stated in the Discussion and the 23% stated in the Results for the M2 model under IPTA DR3.

The numerical audit discusses pulsar counts only and does not mention the 24% vs 23% inconsistency for IPTA DR3/M2. No reviewer comment specifically flags the summary-body mismatch in that probability value.
The reviewer did not comment on the specific probability values or the numerical inconsistency between the Discussion and Results sections for the IPTA DR3 dataset.

The mathematical consistency audit explicitly passes items related to Eq. (5) and the -3/8 exponent but never audits the appended limit claim 'lim_{tau_a -> tau_c} f_orb^(P,a) = 0' in Eq. (forbP-a). No reviewer comment challenges this false asymptotic statement.

In the mathematical consistency audit, Eq. (5) is marked PASS and there is no mention of Eq. (forbP-a) having an incorrect limit as tau_a approaches tau_c. The injected false asymptotic claim was therefore not detected.

The reviewer explicitly audited the relevant mathematical derivation in the 'Mathematical consistency audit' and gave it a 'PASS' verdict, failing to identify the false limit appended to the equation.

The reviewer flags a typographical error in the Introduction ('proving' vs 'probing') but does not flag the homophone swap 'affect' for 'effect' in the Methods sentence about binary mass ratio and detection efficiency. The minor issue about mass ratio (item 2 under Minor issues) discusses the substance of the q=1 assumption but does not mention the 'affect/effect' typo.

The reviewer flags a different typo in the Introduction ('proving') but does not mention the homophone error 'negligible affect' in Sec. III. The nearby mass-ratio comment addresses scientific justification, not the specific typo.
The reviewer quoted the sentence containing the error in Minor Issue 2 but used the correct spelling 'effect' and did not flag the 'affect' typo as an issue.
